action: The instructor presents the chapter agenda on a slide.
why: To introduce the topics before the practical work.

action: The instructor displays an introduction to how surface appearance characterizes the model.
why: To explain the role of shading and texturing.

action: The slide changes from the introduction to a three-part workflow overview.
why: To set up the sequence before showing its individual passes.

action: The instructor shows a slide listing common PBR maps and their uses.
why: To explain how surface maps describe material response across lighting and applications.

action: The presentation switches from Node Wrangler to the Poly Haven add-on.
why: To identify helpers used during node and texture work.

action: The artist surveys the character and its expanded object hierarchy before tidying.
view: solid user orthographic front view with geometry nodes and modifier panels
why: To prepare the project for material assignment and subsequent lookup.
reader_equivalent: scene_tree() and inspect the character hierarchy

action: The artist batch-renames selected character objects, first replacing a name fragment and then selecting prefix mode.
view: solid user orthographic front view and rename dialog
why: To give related objects consistent identifiable names.
reader_equivalent: Use bpy object names while preserving the skill's required object names

action: The artist selects separate hair curves in the Outliner and inspects their modifier stacks and node-group names.
why: To match hair geometry-node names with the owning objects.
reader_equivalent: Set the relevant modifier node_group.name from its owning object's name using bpy

action: The artist collapses the organized hair hierarchy and selects the body to inspect its vertex groups.
why: To locate leftover groups no longer needed after retopology.
reader_equivalent: Inspect obj.vertex_groups and remove only groups known to be unused

action: The artist removes remaining unused vertex groups from clothing objects one by one.
why: To clean up construction data before shading.
reader_equivalent: Remove verified unused entries from obj.vertex_groups with bpy

action: The artist displays a text-editor checklist for basic materials, texture creation, and procedural enhancement.
view: full character in solid orthographic view beside text editor
why: To keep the shading passes ordered from broad colors to detail.

action: The artist uses the modifier input context menu to paste a driver onto another hair section and then selects the ponytail.
tool: Geometry Nodes modifier and driver context menu
view: close front and three-quarter character view with node editor
why: To synchronize the hair viewport-density control across sections.
reader_equivalent: Use bpy drivers on the appropriate modifier interface input

action: The artist copies the active object's empty material setup to selected objects and checks that the colored UV checker disappears.
tool: Material Properties copy material to selected
view: front and oblique material-preview character views
why: To clear the temporary checker before basic material work.
reader_equivalent: Remove temporary checker slots from the selected meshes with bpy

action: The artist works through scalp visibility controls in the Outliner while the hair remains visible.
why: To hide the scalp carriers without hiding their generated hair.
reader_equivalent: Set the appropriate scalp object visibility properties with bpy

action: The artist experiments with the skin base color, splits the viewport, and changes the new area to an Image Editor.
why: To keep the reference available when choosing the skin color.
reader_equivalent: Set Principled BSDF Base Color using a visually selected reference color

action: The artist checks assigned hair colors, rotates to the ponytail, and creates a named material for its band.
view: material preview with reference swatches, then close rear hair view
why: To give the hair accessory its own editable surface.
reader_equivalent: Create a bpy material and assign it to Hair.Band

action: The artist lowers gum and tooth roughness while inspecting the isolated mouth close up.
view: isolated mouth in material preview with swatch image
why: To produce glossier wet-looking mouth surfaces.
reader_equivalent: Set each mouth material's Principled Roughness input

action: The artist opens the gum material's subsurface section and increases its weight while watching the mouth preview.
why: To give the gums a softer translucent response to light.
reader_equivalent: Set the gum Principled BSDF Subsurface Weight input

action: The artist zooms from the rendered face into the isolated eyeballs and begins adding material slots.
view: Cycles rendered preview, isolated eyeballs, reference swatches
why: To establish separate surfaces for the eye regions.
reader_equivalent: Add sclera, iris and pupil materials to the eye mesh

action: The artist selects the pupil material and enters eye mesh Edit Mode to select its central region.
tool: Mesh Edit Mode and material slots
why: To assign a separate dark material to the pupil faces.
reader_equivalent: Assign the pupil material index to the selected eye polygons with bpy

action: The artist rotates to inspect the hair and opens the character concept beside the rendered model.
view: rendered profile close-up with concept image
why: To compare hair root darkness against the design.
reader_equivalent: Use render_image and compare_images to inspect hair against the reference

action: The artist previews Curves Info Intercept on the hair and searches for a Color Ramp in the Shader Editor.
view: rendered hair close-up beside Shader Editor
why: To visualize and adjust the root-to-tip gradient.
reader_equivalent: Connect ShaderNodeHairInfo Intercept to a ShaderNodeValToRGB factor

action: The artist adds a color input node beside the intercept ramp while previewing the grayscale hair gradient.
tool: Shader Editor Color node and Color Ramp
view: rendered profile close-up and expanded shader nodes
why: To prepare the existing hair color for combination with the gradient.
reader_equivalent: Create a ShaderNodeRGB and combine its color with the intercept ramp

action: The artist inspects the colored hair shader and opens render properties before switching to a hair-specific shader.
why: To judge the strand material in the intended rendering engine.
reader_equivalent: Set scene.render.engine to CYCLES and inspect the hair with render_image

action: The artist switches the material output between Principled Hair BSDF and Principled BSDF while the rendered preview resolves.
why: To compare how the two shaders light the same hair color.
reader_equivalent: Build each shader branch and compare Cycles renders

action: The artist reconnects the hair shader and switches to material preview to inspect its different appearance.
tool: Principled Hair BSDF and Material Output
view: head close-up in rendered and material-preview shading
why: To demonstrate why a separate Eevee preview branch is useful.
reader_equivalent: Use separate Cycles and Eevee Material Output targets

action: The artist duplicates the brow material branch, targets one output to Cycles, and replaces its Principled shader with Principled Hair BSDF.
view: close rendered eye and brow with shader nodes
why: To retain a separate fast-preview material while using hair shading in Cycles.
reader_equivalent: Create targeted ShaderNodeOutputMaterial nodes and connect appropriate BSDFs

action: The artist rotates and zooms from the finished hair and brow preview to the eyes.
view: Cycles rendered front and three-quarter face
why: To judge hair before beginning the eye shader.
reader_equivalent: Render the character face in Cycles after assigning the hair material

action: The artist connects UV coordinates to a Mapping node for the iris gradient and splits the workspace for UV inspection.
view: isolated rendered eye beside Shader Editor
why: To align the procedural iris with its UV layout.
reader_equivalent: Connect ShaderNodeTexCoord UV to ShaderNodeMapping Vector

action: The artist adds and moves Color Ramp stops while watching a black-edged grayscale iris ring.
tool: Spherical Gradient Texture and Color Ramp
view: isolated eye render, shader and UV editors
why: To fit the inner and outer iris boundaries to the eye geometry.
reader_equivalent: Adjust the spherical-gradient Color Ramp stops while checking a rendered eye

action: The artist pastes a pink iris color into the ramp and compares interpolation modes in the preview.
view: isolated eye close-up with Shader Editor and UV Editor
why: To choose a smooth transition between iris color and the dark rim.
reader_equivalent: Set ramp colors and interpolation through bpy

action: The artist adds another iris ramp stop and lightens a copy of the pink color.
view: isolated eye close-up and zoomed shader node
why: To introduce a lighter band inside the iris.
reader_equivalent: Add a lighter Color Ramp element using bpy

action: The artist checks the colored iris at different zoom levels and reframes the node network for additional variation.
view: isolated rendered eye and UV layout
why: To assess the ring before adding finer variation.
reader_equivalent: Render the isolated eye and inspect the ramp-driven iris

action: The artist makes a second gradient linear, adds a ramp, and previews its mask on the iris.
tool: Linear Gradient Texture and Color Ramp
view: isolated eye in front orthographic view with Shader Editor
why: To build a directional darkening mask for the upper iris.
reader_equivalent: Connect a linear ShaderNodeTexGradient to a Color Ramp

action: The artist observes a diagonally split iris mask and opens the editor selector to inspect UV alignment.
why: To correct the mismatch between the intended vertical shading and the UV orientation.
reader_equivalent: Inspect and rotate the iris UV island as needed before evaluating the gradient

action: The artist connects the layered iris color into the Principled shader and inspects the result close up.
view: isolated eye render with selected iris UV ring
why: To turn the layered color preview into the actual iris surface.
reader_equivalent: Link the combined color socket to Principled BSDF Base Color

action: The artist selects the pupil material and deletes its Principled shader, leaving the output unconnected in the displayed frame.
view: isolated eye close-up and iris UV ring
why: To remove the pupil's visible surface reflection.
reader_equivalent: For a black non-reflecting pupil use the stage's black emission material

action: The artist lowers the sclera roughness and rotates the isolated eyeballs to inspect them.
view: isolated eyeballs front and oblique rendered views
why: To adjust the eye-white highlights before adding the cornea.
reader_equivalent: Set the sclera Principled Roughness input and inspect from multiple views

action: The artist creates and names a new material on the separate cornea sphere.
why: To build an independent transparent surface over the eyeball.
reader_equivalent: Create and assign a named cornea material to the enclosing sphere

action: The artist examines the transmissive cornea and switches the render engine from Cycles to Eevee for preview setup.
view: isolated reflective cornea in material preview
why: To configure a usable real-time preview of the clear eye shell.
reader_equivalent: Set the cornea shader transmission and roughness, disable shadow visibility, and configure Eevee ray tracing

action: Opens Batch Rename on the two selected cornea objects and switches the type to find/replace to fix the left/right suffix.
view: Layout workspace, Object Mode, hair and eyes in material-less solid view
why: Both eyes need distinct left/right names so their materials stay separate.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: obj.name = obj.name.replace(old, new) per object

action: Checks the renamed eyes in rendered view, flips the Render Engine back to Cycles and looks at the noisy preview.
tool: Viewport shading menu (Z pie), Properties > Render
view: front orthographic, zoomed onto the face
why: Confirm the eye material reads correctly in Cycles.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: scene.render.engine='CYCLES'; render_image from front

action: Zooms out to the full body in solid view and opens a text note listing the three planned passes: basic materials, textures, procedural enhancement.
view: front orthographic full body, grey solid shading
why: Marks the shift from flat blockout materials to image-based texturing.

action: Adds an Image Texture node to the body skin material and fills the New Image dialog: name jenny_skin_color_map, alpha on, blank type, then types 4096 in width.
tool: Shader Editor > Image Texture > New Image
view: front orthographic body with node editor and UV image editor open
why: A dedicated paintable colour map for the skin.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: bpy.data.images.new('jenny_skin_color_map',4096,4096,alpha=True); add ShaderNodeTexImage, assign image, link Color->Base Color

action: In Texture Paint with Paint Soft, picks highlight, darker and reddish skin tones from the colour picker and adds each to a palette named skin.
tool: Texture Paint > Paint Soft, Color Picker + Color Palette
view: front orthographic face with UV image editor beside
why: A reusable set of skin tones for painting.
reader_equivalent: Hex values are sample colours; exec_python can store them as palette via bpy.data.palettes.new('skin') and colors.new()

action: Fills the whole skin image back to the base tone with Fill, then in Edit Mode selects face patches and uses Select Linked to isolate the head.
tool: Texture Paint Fill; Edit Mode face select, L select linked
view: front then right orthographic, mesh selection shown in UV editor
why: Isolate regions so paint can be masked or re-based without touching the rest.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: set polygon.select by region / use paint mask via bpy.ops.paint.face_select_toggle

action: Paints a white band with Paint Soft under the eye, then switches to the Blur brush to smear it, adjusting radius with F.
view: close-up front 3/4 of the nose and cheek
why: Test whether blur can soften painted edges; narrator says it works poorly.

action: Sped-up soft painting of nose and nostril colour at a close zoom, using F to resize the brush often and Shift+Alt to orbit.
view: User Perspective (Local) nose close-up; reference photo overlay on the right
why: Build nostril shading and warm nose tone by hand from the reference.

action: Paints the lip colour at a small brush, dark mouth line then lighter lower lip, and undoes one stroke.
view: orthographic lips extreme close-up; UV window shows lip shapes
why: Fine lip colour needs a tiny radius.

action: Paints the ear with Paint Soft, radius changed by F, Shift held to orbit, then jumps to a profile view of the earlobe.
view: side view of the ear, local perspective
why: Add warm colour in ear folds.

action: Paints toes and soles on the colour map, first in 3D, then in the image editor full-screen with Ctrl+Space, reddening the toe tips.
view: foot close-up then maximised UV image editor
why: Warm tint on toe edges is easier to place on the flat UV island.
reader_equivalent: exec_python alternative: bake vertex paint; no direct equivalent

action: Continues in the maximised UV editor on the fingertip islands, dabbing warm colour at the tips, then returns to 3D.
view: maximised UV image editor, then side view of arm
why: Colour at the ends of fingers gives life.

action: Paints the hand: palm and finger colour with Paint Soft at varying radius while orbiting with Shift.
why: Add tonal variation on palm and fingers.

action: Lowers strength to paint shading on the legs and knees; a Hue/Saturation/Value node (Sat 1.04, Value 1.1) now sits in front of Base Color.
tool: Texture Paint > Paint Soft + HSV node
view: orthographic front and back of legs
why: Subtle knee warming at lower strength.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: add ShaderNodeHueSaturation with Saturation 1.04 Value 1.1 between image and Base Color

action: Creates a jenny_shirt_color_map image, then a brown-painted shirt appears, a plane is added to hold the concept sheet, and a node-image reference board is shown.
view: front orthographic full body, then a reference board
why: Separate colour maps per garment.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: bpy.data.images.new('jenny_shirt_color_map',..)

action: Starts the skirt/shirt area: orbits the character, adds a plane next to it to hold the reference (Shift+A), checks right and perspective views of the skirt pleats.
view: right orthographic then perspective close-up of skirt
why: Check pleat shape before painting skirt colour.

action: In the UV editor selects loose islands of the skirt and moves them within the layout to resize the waistband pieces.
why: Tidy the UV layout before painting.

action: Paints the shoe straps with Paint Soft at 44-52px, orbiting around the strap.
view: close-up of shoe strap with UV map showing strap island
why: Dark brown strap colour.

action: Skin painting finished; reviews nose, lips and ear, switches to Cycles rendered view, then saves.
why: Finish skin painting and check in render.

action: Switches to Object Mode and orbits the character after saying the painting is enough for now; shows colour maps exist for skin, shirt, skirt, trousers.
view: front perspective full body with shader editor
why: Close the colour map step.

action: Turns the viewport to grey/flat shading to show Multires and Mirror modifier stack, then back to colour.
view: front orthographic full body, solid grey then material
why: Reason: a Multires can be baked to a normal map if the model leaves Blender.

action: Previews the Geometry node Pointiness socket with Ctrl+Shift+click, jumping through sockets until the right one shows; checks Cycles.
view: front orthographic upper body with Shader editor
why: Pointiness input only works in Cycles.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: add ShaderNodeNewGeometry, link Pointiness to a ColorRamp

action: Adds a Color Ramp on Pointiness, crunches the black stop to about 0.4 and brings the white stop in so the effect is visible.
why: Make pointiness contrast visible.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position=0.40; elements[1].position=0.89

action: Fills the second color ramp stop settings (pos 0.548), then adds an Image Texture with New Image for the pointiness map at 4096 px, set to Non-Color.
tool: Shader Editor > Image Texture > New Image
why: Grayscale data map, no colour involved.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: images.new(...,4096,4096); image.colorspace_settings.name='Non-Color'

action: Selects the shirt, selects the new image node, opens Render properties and scrolls down to the Bake panel.
view: front orthographic shirt in rendered view
why: Bake target must be the active image node.

action: Sets Bake Type to Emission and target Image Textures, Clear Image on, margin 16 px Adjacent Faces, then bakes; viewport shows the shirt emitting.
why: Bake pointiness through the emission of the material output.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: bpy.ops.object.bake(type='EMIT', margin=16, margin_type='ADJACENT_FACES')

action: Inspects the baked pointiness map in the Image Editor, deletes the temporary nodes, selects the Multires modifier in preparation for the normal bake.
view: front orthographic; Image Editor showing the baked shirt UV layout
why: Confirm bake before dropping the helper nodes.

action: Selects a new image node named normal_map, sets Bake Type to Normal (Space Tangent, swizzle +X +Y +Z) and presses Bake; the result is a purple normal map.
view: front orthographic upper body, then viewport turns lilac
why: Capture Multires detail onto a normal map.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: bpy.ops.object.bake(type='NORMAL', normal_space='TANGENT'); then save image

action: Connects the baked normal map through a Normal Map node, compares front/side views and turns the Multires modifier off to show detail persists.
tool: Shader Editor Normal Map node, Modifiers
view: front and 3/4 side views of shirt
why: Check the normal bake gives the same wrinkles as Multires.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: add ShaderNodeNormalMap; link image Color -> Normal Map Color -> BSDF Normal

action: Finds clipping where the shirt meets an armpit, enters Sculpt Mode with the Grab brush and pulls the surface out with Subdivision at level 1.
view: side zoom of upper arm, local perspective
why: Fix clipping after the normal bake so Multires is not needed.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes with Grab-like push on the clipped region

action: Orbits (F adjusts radius, Shift+Alt orbit) and pulls out the shirt sections with Grab at radius ~390 px, then returns to Object Mode.
view: close-up front chest, then full body in object mode
why: Remove the clipping areas and verify the normal map stays correct.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes: move vertices outward near sleeve opening

action: Adds a Mix node to the shirt material: colour map into A, pointiness into B, then opens the Blend Mode dropdown.

settings.Blend options listed: Mix, Darken, Multiply, Color Burn, Lighten, Screen, Overlay, Soft Light...

why: Combine the painted colour with the baked pointiness.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: ShaderNodeMix data_type RGBA; link colour->A, pointiness->B

action: Selects Multiply as the blend mode and drags the Factor slider while watching the shirt, settling near 0.4.
why: Darken creases without losing colour.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: mix.blend_type='MULTIPLY'; mix.inputs[0].default_value=0.4

action: Plugs the Multiply result into Principled BSDF Base Color, then zooms to the shirt in perspective to judge the darker folds.
tool: Shader Editor link to Base Color
why: Finished colour+pointiness base ready for fabric texture.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: links.new(mix.outputs[2], bsdf.inputs['Base Color'])

action: Copies a Poly Haven fabric material node group from the asset browser (Ctrl+C) and pastes it into the shirt shader, then moves it near the BSDF.
tool: Asset Browser (Poly Haven Fetch Assets), Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V nodes
view: front perspective with asset browser open
why: Bring in PBR maps without replacing existing shirt colour (drag-on-object would overwrite).
reader_equivalent: Poly Haven add-on not usable; load stand-in images with exec_python

action: Adds a second Mix node with Overlay blend (Factor around 0.5) so the base colour tints the fabric texture, then lowers the factor to 0.044.
view: close-up of shirt with painted details
why: Overlay keeps fabric texture while showing painted colour.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: mix.blend_type='OVERLAY'; Factor tuned by eye

action: Pulls the pasted fabric texture nodes into the shirt tree, drags the others downward and places the baked normal map node among them.
why: Organise nodes so both normal maps are available.

action: Tidies node layout then searches for a Vector node with the Add dialog to mix two normal maps (typed 'vect').
why: Combine baked normal with the fabric normal.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: add ShaderNodeVectorMath or mix vectors for normals

action: Shows a Poly Haven leather sphere test, then applies the skirt material and moves to bake pointiness for the skirt.
why: Leather for the skirt; bake pointiness as with shirt.

action: Bakes pointiness for the skirt (Bake Type Emission), flips the image editor to the pointiness map to inspect it and spots a small error.
view: front perspective skirt then Image Editor
why: Same recipe as for the shirt applied to the skirt.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: bpy.ops.object.bake(type='EMIT')

action: Saves the skirt pointiness image after inspecting its baked islands.
why: Preserve the curvature bake.
reader_equivalent: Save the baked image with bpy image.save().

action: Duplicates the image texture node and opens a new image dialog for the skirt.
why: Prepare a separate bake target for normals.
reader_equivalent: Create a 4096-square image and assign it to an active Image Texture node.

action: Connects the skirt normal image through a Normal Map node into the Principled shader.
why: Restore the baked surface detail in shading.
reader_equivalent: Connect Non-Color image Color to Normal Map Color, then Normal to Principled Normal.

action: Selects the skirt straps and changes the bake type from Normal to Emission while viewing the existing skirt map.
why: Add the separate straps to the existing pointiness image without erasing the prior bake.
reader_equivalent: Set emission bake and disable use_clear before baking the selected straps.

action: Checks the skirt result, selects the boots and starts arranging their shader nodes.
why: Repeat the curvature and normal workflow on footwear.
reader_equivalent: Select the boot material and construct a Geometry Pointiness to Color Ramp bake setup.

action: Adjusts the pointiness ramp while orbiting around the boots, then opens a new bake image dialog.
why: Tune crease contrast before recording a boot pointiness texture.
reader_equivalent: Set ramp stops by inspecting the boot and create an active bake image.

action: Combines the boot color image and baked pointiness image with a Multiply mix node.
why: Add crease shading to the painted leather color.
reader_equivalent: Link color and pointiness textures to a Multiply color mix and connect its result to base color.

action: Inspects the boot from the side and returns the combined image to the full material preview.
why: Judge how the combined color reads on the finished material.
reader_equivalent: Connect the mixed texture to Principled Base Color and render a preview.

action: Inspects an abnormally multicolored boot normal bake and opens the modifier stack.
why: Identify the active Mirror modifier as a potential bake problem.
reader_equivalent: Inspect and temporarily disable the Mirror modifier during the bake.

action: Views the rebaked boot normal material from several angles and notices dark strap regions.
why: Check for gaps where the separate straps were not included in the image.
reader_equivalent: Render the shoe and inspect the map coverage before baking the other object.

action: Enables Clear Image, selects the shoe and its normal-map target, and starts another bake.
why: Replace the incomplete normal bake before adding the straps.
reader_equivalent: Set use_clear true and bake the shoe to its active image node.

action: Reviews the rebaked shoes, restores the mirror and adds a subdivision modifier.
why: Return to a smooth mirrored display after baking.
reader_equivalent: Restore Mirror and add a subdivision surface modifier with viewport level 1.

action: Joins the footwear components with matching modifiers and inspects the skirt straps.
why: Consolidate components that can share the same modifier arrangement.
reader_equivalent: Select compatible components with the intended active object and use bpy.ops.object.join().

action: Rearranges the skirt shader and adds vector math nodes alongside two normal-map branches.
why: Combine the normal contributions from baked folds and material detail.
reader_equivalent: Use Vector Math Add followed by Normalize for the normal branches.

action: Zooms out to assess the character, then isolates the jaw object.
why: Move from clothing to the tongue, teeth and gums.
reader_equivalent: Isolate the jaw object for a close material preview.

action: Feeds a ramped Voronoi pattern into a Bump node and previews its normal effect on the tongue.
why: Make fine tongue surface texture.
reader_equivalent: Connect Voronoi through Color Ramp to Bump Height and Bump Normal to Principled Normal.

action: Mixes Noise and the ramped Voronoi pattern at half strength and routes the result toward roughness.
why: Introduce varied tongue surface reflectivity.
reader_equivalent: Combine noise and ramp output with Multiply and connect to shader Roughness.

action: Increases the tongue Voronoi scale and reduces Bump strength while checking a close preview.
why: Keep tongue relief fine rather than exaggerated.
reader_equivalent: Adjust Voronoi Scale and lower Bump Strength while checking the rendered tongue.

action: Inspects the white teeth material and zooms back to view the whole mouth.
why: Check the simple tooth material against tongue and gums.
reader_equivalent: Assign a light Principled material to the teeth slot and inspect the isolated mouth.

action: Returns to the complete character and selects the body material.
why: Begin the skin-specific shading pass.
reader_equivalent: Select the body and open its skin material node tree.

action: Adds a Geometry node and Color Ramp and previews the skin pointiness output.
view: front full character and node editor
why: Prepare a skin curvature map despite the absence of Multires on this mesh.
reader_equivalent: Connect Geometry Pointiness to a Color Ramp and bake its emission to an image.

action: Removes the temporary curvature nodes and inserts a Mix node between the skin color and baked pointiness images.
view: isolated full body and skin image
why: Combine the baked curvature with the original skin color.
reader_equivalent: Connect the color map and pointiness texture to a color mix.

action: Previews the body with the pointiness multiply blend and returns to the clothed character.
why: Set a restrained contribution from the curvature image.
reader_equivalent: Use a Multiply color mix with a roughly 0.265 factor as an observed starting point.

action: Previews a separate transparent tattoo image, which appears black outside painted areas.
view: front character and transparent checkerboard image
why: Prepare an independent layer for skin markings.
reader_equivalent: Create an RGBA image with transparent background and an Image Texture node.

action: Enters Texture Paint and draws loose green and blue marks along the arm on the transparent image.
why: Demonstrate a separate editable tattoo layer.
reader_equivalent: Paint into the separate RGBA image in UV space and save it.

action: Adds a Mix Color node to combine the tattoo image with the skin color.
why: Use tattoo alpha to limit the overlay to painted pixels.
reader_equivalent: Connect tattoo Alpha to mix Factor, skin to A, tattoo Color to B.

action: Connects the layered color to the skin shader, reviews the colored arm marks, then mutes the demonstration layer.
why: Check the overlay and temporarily remove example marks.
reader_equivalent: Connect the mix to Principled Base Color and mute or remove the demonstration mix.

action: Previews a Layer Weight Facing mask through a B-Spline Color Ramp and adds a color mix.
why: Create view-dependent edge tint for the skin.
reader_equivalent: Connect Facing to a B-Spline ramp and use it to blend an edge tint into skin color.

action: Frames the existing color network and zooms close to the face before adding a noise texture.
why: Start a fine skin-color variation layer.
reader_equivalent: Add a UV-driven Noise Texture and ramp it before mixing into the skin color.

action: Adjusts high-frequency noise and ramp stops while comparing the black-and-white skin mask at two zoom levels.
why: Control the density and contrast of small color flecks.
reader_equivalent: Use UV Mapping into Noise and adjust a Color Ramp while inspecting the result.

action: Groups the color variation nodes in a labeled frame while viewing the face.
view: front facial close-up and shader graph
why: Keep the material graph understandable as it grows.
reader_equivalent: Parent the variation nodes to a labeled NodeFrame.

action: Adjusts a Voronoi-driven ramp and checks the skin at face and mouth scale.
why: Tune a second fine skin variation and identify unwanted mottling on the lips.
reader_equivalent: Connect Voronoi Distance to a ramp and inspect the skin and lips.

action: Renames a color attribute in the mesh data while in Vertex Paint.
view: front face and mesh data properties
why: Create a paintable mask for controlling skin variation.
reader_equivalent: Create a mesh color attribute for the skin-variation mask.

action: Adjusts the variation ramp and inspects the masked skin around the lips before arranging the shader graph.
why: Keep the procedural variation adjustable and control its lip coverage.
reader_equivalent: Use the painted color attribute to mask the noise variation.

action: Adjusts the roughness mix while comparing the face and lips in material preview.
why: Control shine separately from the skin variation.
reader_equivalent: Mix the ramped roughness using the color attribute mask and connect to Principled Roughness.

action: Previews a bump branch as a false-color normal and zooms in on the mouth.
why: Inspect the pore relief and confirm that the lip region should be smooth.
reader_equivalent: Connect the masked texture to Bump Height and inspect the normal output.

action: Lowers bump strength and reconnects the bump output to the skin shader before inspecting the face.
view: face close-up, false-color and material preview
why: Reduce excessive pore relief.
reader_equivalent: Set Bump strength around 0.235 and connect its Normal to Principled Normal.

action: Adjusts skin subsurface weight and begins changing the scale while checking a Cycles preview.
why: Reduce the washed-out appearance caused by overly broad scattering.
